question.problem:
In a particular shop, cables are sold in coils. The length of the cable in a coil is normally distributed with a mean of $50\,\text{m}$ and a standard deviation of $0.7\,\text{m}.$ If John bought $5$ coils, what is the probability that the total length of the cables he bought is greater than $250\,\text{m}$ and less than $253\,m?$ You may assume that the lengths of the cable in the coils are mutually independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.7\,$ | $\,0.9554\,$ | $\,0.9564\,$ | $\,0.9573\,$ | $\,0.9582\,$ |
| $\,1.8\,$ | $\,0.9641\,$ | $\,0.9649\,$ | $\,0.9656\,$ | $\,0.9664\,$ |
| $\,1.9\,$ | $\,0.9713\,$ | $\,0.9719\,$ | $\,0.9726\,$ | $\,0.9732\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let ${X}_{i}$ denote the length of cable in the $i$th coil. Then, we have

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(50,{0.7}^{2}),\,1\le i\le 5.
$$

Let the random variable $L$ denote the total length of the cables in $5$ randomly selected coils. Then, since

$$
L={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{5},
$$

we have that $L$ is normally distributed, where

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[L] & =5\cdot 50 \\  & =250, \\ \text{Var}[L] & =5\cdot {0.7}^{2} \\  & =2.45.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
L∼N(250,2.45).
$$

In order to find $P(250<L<253),$ we convert $L$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(250<L<253) & =P(\frac{250-250}{\sqrt{2.45}}<Z<\frac{253-250}{\sqrt{2.45}}) \\  & ≈P(0<Z<1.92) \\  & =Φ(1.92)-Φ(0) \\  & =Φ(1.92)-0.5\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(1.92)≈0.9726.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(250<L<253) & ≈Φ(0.95)-0.5 \\  & ≈0.4726.\end{aligned}
$$
